name: Visual Discomfort from Building Frontages
description:
Faithful replication of the human rating task in Penacchio, O., Otazu, X., Wilkins, A. J., & Haigh, S. M. (2023). A mechanistic account of visual discomfort. Frontiers in Neuroscience, 17, 1200661. https://doi.org/10.3389/fnins.2023.1200661 (architecture image sets first rated in Penacchio & Wilkins, 2015, Vision Research, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.visres.2014.12.013).

What participants do: participants are randomly assigned to one of the two sets of 74 colour photographs of building frontages (Architecture 1 or Architecture 2). They see every photograph of their set once, in random order and for as long as they like, and rate how uncomfortable it is to look at on a 7-point scale from 1 = "not uncomfortable at all" to 7 = "very uncomfortable". The instructions say explicitly that discomfort is meant, not unpleasantness, ugliness or dislike. Then age, gender and viewing device.

Original finding: images that observers rated as uncomfortable produced, in a neurodynamic model of early visual cortex, larger overall activation, a less sparse response and a more unbalanced distribution of activity across orientations; raising the model's excitation-to-inhibition ratio shifted all images toward the uncomfortable profile. Per-image mean discomfort ratings can be compared with the authors' published image metrics on Zenodo.

Stimuli: the authors' photographs from Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10065026, CC0), used with credit. This template is removed if the authors object.

Differences from the original study: (1) Online instead of in the lab on a calibrated display (original: 720 × 960 px images, 15° visual angle, 80 cm viewing distance); a question on the viewing device is added. (2) The TIFF images are converted to JPEG, and the red slide numbers printed in the top-left corner of the released files are removed. (3) Instruction wording is paraphrased from the paper's description; a short warning for people prone to migraine is added. (4) The two abstract-art sets of the paper (rated on a 5-point scale) are not included.

elements.description: One row per photograph (key = file name, e.g. arch1_07 = image 7 of Architecture 1, the image numbers of the authors' data files). All 74 photographs of the assigned set in random order, unlimited viewing time; discomfort 1 = not uncomfortable at all … 7 = very uncomfortable. The authors averaged ratings per image and related them to image statistics (Fourier residuals, model activation, sparseness, orientation isotropy).
